Seed of the Posterior Simulation of a VAR or VEC Model

Source: R/add_seed.R
add_seed.bvarmodel.Rd

The methods of add_seed for VAR and VEC models: they set the seed with which the posterior is simulated, in element seed of object$model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bvarmodel'
add_seed(object, seed, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bvecmodel'
add_seed(object, seed, ...)

Arguments

object

an object of class 'bvarmodel' or 'bvecmodel'.

seed

a non-negative whole number no larger than .Machine$integer.max.

...

not used.

Value

object with the seed set.

Details

write_to_hdf5 writes the seed as attribute seed of group /model, where the BayesTS executable reads it, and the internal samplers of add_posterior_coefficients draw with it too, so a model with a given seed gives the same draws however R's generator stands. So do the simulations that follow the coefficients: add_posterior_forecasts, scenarios included, add_predictive_loglik, add_sign_restrictions and add_sign_zero_restrictions. Each of these three stages – the forecast, the predictive score and the rotations – draws from a seed of its own derived from the model's, as the BayesTS command line seeds its stages from /model/seed, so that a forecast repeated gives the same draws and does not reuse the random numbers the chain started from. A model without a seed draws from R's generator as it stands throughout. BayesTS and this package use different generators, so the same seed gives different draws in the two. A list of models is numbered by the method of bayests.

See also

Other posterior simulation: add_forecast_input.bvarmodel(), add_forecast_input.bvecmodel(), add_posterior_coefficients.bvarmodel(), add_posterior_coefficients.bvecmodel(), add_posterior_forecasts.bvarmodel(), add_posterior_forecasts.bvecmodel(), add_posterior_loglik.bvarmodel(), add_posterior_loglik.bvecmodel(), bvar(), bvec(), predict.bvecmodel()

Examples

# Load data
data("e1")
e1 <- diff(log(e1)) * 100

# Generate model
model <- create_bvarmodel(data = e1, p = 2, iterations = 100, burnin = 50)

# Set the seed of the posterior simulation
model <- add_seed(model, 20260916)
model[["model"]][["seed"]]
#> [1] 20260916
